grand_strategy.reading:
The Houthis are the clearest case in the atlas of a small actor that turned a
distant war into leverage over world shipping, and 2026 is the year in which
that leverage reached its culminating point. The Gaza war gave them a
justification, an audience and a free hand against the one trade route that
ties Asia to Europe; the 2025 US and Israeli campaigns cost them ports,
ministers and a chief of staff but not the capacity to hurt; the Iran war and
the closing of Hormuz then made Bab al-Mandab the only maritime outlet of the
Gulf, and on 3-11 September 2026 they took the whole Yemeni coast and Mayyun
to sit on it. In Luttwak's terms the movement has gone past the point where
each further success buys proportionally more: it has stretched its lines
into districts it cannot hold with consent, turned the Saudi restraint of
2022-25 into a Saudi-run coalition, and made the Kingdom an enemy it cannot
pay off, while the patron whose war created the opening is negotiating with
Washington. What it can still do is keep the threat of closure alive and
sell its absence, which is precisely what it did between the Gaza ceasefire
and July 2026 and what it needs to restore. Signals that are not rows: Iran's
foreign minister said in March that Tehran did not need its allies to join
its self-defence, the Houthis stayed out of the June 2025 war and waited four
weeks in 2026 before firing on Israel, and the Houthi leadership told China
and Russia their ships were not targets. All of it shows an actor that
chooses its wars; the open question for the autumn of 2026 is whether it
still can.

stances.note: Each side seeks the other's end: the Houthis, who took Sanaa in September 2014 and rule it as Yemen's authority, pushed in 2026 to take the whole Red Sea coast and are moving on Taiz and Marib; the government (Aden, Presidential Leadership Council under Rashad al-Alimi) announced Operation Dawn on 4 October 2026 and vows to 'liberate Sanaa', while its forces say the aim is to eliminate the Houthi threat. Truce-era deals exist (a 1,680-detainee prisoner swap signed 14 May 2026, now postponed) but do not change the structure; the 2022 truce is dead. Bond - grievance: a twelve-year civil war, executions after 'espionage' trials (19 death sentences on 17 May 2026) and, on the Houthi side, the claim that the government is a Saudi creature. The grade is the one named in the brief, supported by sources that describe a war of mutual elimination; confidence B.
